content.value: Recursive binary search stops when the interval is empty or the midpoint matches. Otherwise, recurse on a strictly smaller half of sorted data. Merge sort stops at a subarray of size zero or one, sorts each half recursively, and merges them. A merge compares the fronts of sorted halves, copies the smaller value, then appends leftovers.

Precondition: a is sorted ascending and the initial interval is 0 through a.length - 1. Excluding mid in the recursive call guarantees progress. Binary search halves the range each step. Merge sort has logarithmically many split levels and linear merging work per level.
Practice: trace the example by hand, change one input, and explain how the result changes. Check an empty or boundary case when the preconditions allow it.
